Release 10.0.0

Date: TBD

Juneau 10.0.0 is a major version release representing a significant milestone for the Apache Juneau project. This release folds in the never-shipped 9.5 development line and also delivers a broad code-quality and maintainability uplift via an extensive SonarQube/SonarLint cleanup pass across the entire codebase.

Major version bump note​

This is the first release in the 10.x line. The jump from 9.x to 10.0 reflects accumulated breaking changes in the API surface and internal architecture that warranted a major version boundary, following Semantic Versioning conventions.

Consumers upgrading from 9.4.x or earlier should consult the V10.0 Migration Guide for a complete list of breaking changes.

Code quality improvements​

This release includes an extensive SonarQube / SonarLint cleanup pass across the entire Juneau codebase, addressing hundreds of code-quality findings including:

  • Removed dead/unreachable code and unused variables.
  • Fixed resource-leak issues (try-with-resources, explicit close calls).
  • Resolved potentially null-dereference paths and improved null-safety.
  • Replaced raw types with proper generic parameterization.
  • Addressed improper exception handling patterns (swallowed exceptions, overly broad catch blocks).
  • Cleaned up redundant casts, unnecessary object creation, and other minor inefficiencies.
  • Suppressed or resolved remaining SonarQube rule violations with documented rationale.

No functional behavior was changed as part of this cleanup; all changes were purely mechanical code-quality improvements.

New Features​

juneau-marshall / juneau-commons​

View-based property projection (@MarshalledProp(view=...))​

Juneau now supports view-based projection: declare named views on bean properties and select an active view per serialize/parse call so only the in-view properties are emitted or consumed. This is the Juneau equivalent of Jackson's @JsonView / MapperFeature.DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION.

Tag a property with one or more string view names via the new view member on @MarshalledProp:

public class Person {
    public String id;                         // untagged — visible in every view

    @MarshalledProp(view = "summary")
    public String name;

    @MarshalledProp(view = "detail")
    public String description;
}

Activate a view on any serializer or parser builder, or override it per call on a session:

// Context-level default:
var s = Json5Serializer.DEFAULT.copy().activeView("summary").build();
s.write(person);  // → {id:'1',name:'Alice'}

// Per-call session override:
s.createSession().activeView("detail").build().write(person);  // → {description:'A person',id:'1'}

Key behaviours:

  • Default-view policy: untagged properties are included in all views by default (mirrors Jackson's DEFAULT_VIEW_INCLUSION=true). Call disableDefaultViewInclusion() to reverse.
  • Union semantics: @MarshalledProp(view = {"A","B"}) makes a property visible when A or B is active.
  • Flat string names: no marker-class hierarchy required.
  • Parse-side: out-of-view input properties are routed through the existing unknown/ignored-property mechanism (silently ignored by default; ignoreUnknownBeanProperties(false) makes them throw).
  • Mix-in support: view membership can be applied to unmodifiable classes via @MarshalledPropApply / applyAnnotations(), just like any other @MarshalledProp attribute.
  • Cross-format: projection is model-level and behaves identically across JSON, XML, HTML, MsgPack, and all other Juneau formats.

See the View-Based Projection topic page for full documentation and a Jackson migration table.

Hibernate lazy-proxy unwrap + JPA cookbook​

Marshalling now deproxifies objects whose runtime class ClassUtils.getProxyFor recognizes, including Hibernate 6/7 lazy association proxies ($HibernateProxy$ in the class name). Serializers use the unwrapped class (immediate superclass for subclass proxies; first interface for JDK proxies) so handler fields and proxy _type names are not emitted. This is a core getClassMetaForObject change across all formats — not a juneau-marshall-hibernate module, and not a parse-into-@Entity feature.

See JPA and Hibernate.

juneau-config / juneau-commons​

Config profiles + relaxed binding (cloud-native environment config)​

Juneau 10.0 adds two Spring-Boot-style ergonomics to the config + settings system, both additive and off-by-default so existing configs are unaffected:

  • Config profiles — a <name>-<profile> overlay (e.g. my-stage.cfg, or my-stage.yml for YAML bases) is merged over the base config when a profile is active. Profile entries win over base, base-only keys survive, and for multiple active profiles the last one wins. Activated via Config.Builder.profiles(...) or the juneau.profiles.active key (system property / env var / config). Resolution happens at the store layer (ProfileConfigStore + ProfileMerge), so variable resolution, format handling, and live reload (a change to the base or any active profile file re-fires change listeners) all behave exactly as for a single-file config. When the Spring Boot bridge is present, juneau.profiles.active piggybacks on Environment.getActiveProfiles() for a single source of truth.
  • Relaxed binding — a single logical config key resolves from any common environment spelling, so k8s-style env vars map cleanly: my.prop / myProp / MySection/myKey are satisfied by MY_PROP / MY_SECTION_MY_KEY. The default Settings env source is wrapped with RelaxedPropertySource (verbatim-first, so exact-match is preserved); it can wrap any other PropertySource too.

See the new Config Profiles & Relaxed Binding topic page for the activation conventions, overlay/merge precedence, and the candidate-generation rules.

juneau-commons / juneau-rest-server​

@ConfigProperties — prefix-scoped whole-object config binding, with RestContext as the pilot​

Juneau 10.0 adds a new @ConfigProperties(prefix = "...") annotation (org.apache.juneau.commons.inject) — Juneau's analog of Spring Boot's @ConfigurationProperties — plus its underlying, independently-callable engine, ConfigPropertiesBinder. Where @Value resolves one configuration value onto one field, @ConfigProperties resolves an entire prefix onto every field of a POJO in one pass:

@ConfigProperties(prefix = "MyService")
public class MyServiceProperties {
    public String host = "localhost";
    public int port = 8080;
}
  • Relaxed key matching by default — reuses RelaxedPropertySource.candidates(...), so MyService.host, MY_SERVICE_HOST, and my.service.host are all equivalent.
  • Same source-chain precedence as @Value — thread-local/global test overrides, then any caller-scoped PropertySource beans, then the process-wide Settings chain (registered sources, system properties, system environment).
  • Nested config objects — a field whose type is itself @ConfigProperties-annotated binds recursively under a sub-prefix.
  • Coexists with @Value/@Inject on the same class — fields owned by either are never touched by the whole-object bind.
  • Auto-registered in the BeanStore — the bound instance is retrievable via beanStore.getBean(...) or plain @Inject anywhere downstream.
  • Current limitations: no Optional<T>/Supplier<T> field types (raw-type conversion only); validation is a no-op extension seam (ConfigPropertiesValidator.NO_OP) reserved for a future release.

Pilot: RestContextProperties. As proof, RestContext's 15 same-prefix RestContext.* env-driven-default @Value fields have been collapsed into a single public @ConfigProperties(prefix = "RestContext") bean, RestContextProperties, retrievable via the new RestContext.getRestContextProperties() or from the resource's BeanStore. Every existing RestContext getter keeps its exact signature and @Rest-annotation-blending behavior — only the source of the underlying default moved. RestContext.uriAuthority/uriContext (a null-vs-empty distinction the binder's raw-type conversion can't express in v1) are unaffected and remain plain @Value fields.

See the new @ConfigProperties Annotation Basics topic page, and the RestContext topic page for the pilot.

@Bean factory-method fixes (juneau-rest-server / juneau-commons). Several @Bean(name=...) factory methods of the same type on a @Rest class now each register their own result. Previously they collapsed into one bean, so @Named("cache") could receive the "db" bean, and health indicators were lost. Each @Bean method is invoked exactly once: overridden methods once, and named framework types such as @Bean(name="encoders") EncoderSet are no longer invoked twice or exported to child resources. @Bean methods may now be protected, package-private or private, matching @Configuration classes. The @Bean("x") value form now matches named framework slots. New: BeanStore.invokeBeanMethod(...) and BeanAnnotation.find(MethodInfo).

juneau-commons / juneau-secret-macos-keychain​

SecretStore SPI — the secure, mutable sibling of PropertySource​

Juneau 10.0 adds a small, JDK-only SecretStore SPI (org.apache.juneau.commons.secret, @since 10.0.0) for storing and retrieving secrets by key — store / find / exists / delete. It is the secure, mutable sibling of PropertySource: values are held as char[] (never String), and are never toString()'d, logged, or dumped.

  • InMemorySecretStore — the zero-config, ConcurrentHashMap-backed, process-local default (honest about being neither persistent nor cross-node), with defensive-copy in/out so callers can zero their own arrays.
  • EnvVarSecretStore — a read-only store backed by System.getenv (store/delete are unsupported).
  • SecretStoreProvider + META-INF/services — ServiceLoader discovery mirroring PropertySourceProvider; opt-in via SecretStores.fromServiceLoader().
  • SecretStores.resolve(beanStore) — resolves the active store from a BeanStore, defaulting to InMemorySecretStore (the BeanStore-with-drop-in-default idiom used elsewhere in the framework).
  • Opt-in Settings bridge — SecretStorePropertySource exposes a chosen store as a PropertySource only where a consumer deliberately wires it, and implements the SensitivePropertySource marker so dump/log/toString() paths redact bridged values. Secrets stay out of the general config/$P{...}/SVL namespace by default.
  • New opt-in module juneau-secret-macos-keychain — a KeychainSecretStore backed by the macOS security keychain CLI, honoring a ReplayCache-style FailMode (fail-open/fail-closed) for backend-unavailable behavior. It lives outside juneau-commons because it shells out to an OS process. store sends the command to security -i on stdin, so the secret never appears on a command line and a JVM started from a terminal is never left waiting on a password prompt. find reads the password from security find-generic-password -g, so secrets containing tabs, other control characters, non-ASCII text, quotes or backslashes come back exactly as stored.

See the Secrets section of the Settings topic page for details.

juneau-commons / juneau-beanquery-sql / juneau-beanquery-postgres​

BeanQuery contexts and sessions​

org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery is a protocol-agnostic API for searching, sorting, projecting and paging rows of beans, in memory or over JDBC. Engines follow a context/session split:

  • Immutable, builder-built contexts. InMemoryBeanQueryContext.create(Person.class)...build() and SqlBeanQueryContext.create(Person.class)...build() fix the columns, operators, limits and a server-side guard once. copy() derives a variant.
  • Per-request sessions. getSession(rows) / getSession(), or createSession()...build() for per-request rules: narrow the columns, override the limits, add a guard, or pass a caller-owned JDBC Connection. A session offers find, findValues, count, stream, streamValues and resolve.
  • Validate before run. Every query is resolved into a ResolvedQuery first. Unknown columns, disallowed operators, over-long search strings, too many clauses or sort keys, and over-deep expressions are rejected with BeanQuerySyntaxException; they are never silently dropped. defaultLimit (100) applies when limit is missing; a limit above maxLimit (1000) is clamped to it, never rejected.
  • Counts by policy. CountPolicy (NONE, MATCHED, BOTH, IF_REQUESTED) decides which counts a Page carries. Page.total()/Page.matched() are independently-optional (see below).
  • Safe regex. $regex is enabled by default; allowRegex(false) disables it. In memory, each call's regex matching shares one regexTimeout deadline (default 50 ms).
  • Engine errors. Failures raise BeanQueryExecutionException (a server error), whose message names no SQL or bind values.
  • SQL engine. Guards are parenthesized and AND-ed into every statement. There are fetch-size and query-timeout settings, and connections come from a DataSource or supplier and are released by the session. stream reads rows lazily and closes its cursor with the stream or the session.
  • DataTables. The juneau-rest-server-datatables adapter runs on the new session API. It asks for counts with CountRequest.BOTH on the query builder and maps length=-1 to maxLimit.
  • BeanQuery.Builder/GroupBuilder. Replace the removed BeanQueryBuilder. Fluent eq/ne/in/contains/prefix/gt/gte/lt/lte/between/regex/op/search conditions, promotable into cross-column $or/$and/$not groups via GroupBuilder. Repeated conditions on the same column built through the fluent API no longer silently overwrite each other — they merge into an implicit $and(...).
  • One resolved search tree. Filter/FilterResolver/FilterEvaluator give the in-memory and SQL engines a single, already-validated search tree to walk instead of each parsing search strings independently.
  • Independently-optional counts. Page.hasTotal() is gone; Page.total()/Page.matched() are OptionalLong, so a caller that did not ask for a count gets an empty OptionalLong back rather than an exception.
  • DataTables global search box + legacy-search parity. The DataTables adapter now maps the global search box to a synthesized $or across searchable columns, each with a leaf chosen by its declared SearchType ($contains for TEXT/ID, $prefix for VERSION, $eqic for ENUM, and $eq conditionally for NUMERIC/BOOLEAN/TIMESTAMP only when the global term parses as that type, otherwise that column is silently skipped) instead of $contains for every column, and reports counts through the OptionalLong pair above.
  • RelativeDuration literals. A signed [+-]<n>(ms|s|m|h|d) wire literal (e.g. -24h for "24 hours ago") round-trips through the builder for TIMESTAMP/duration columns (parity with a common legacy search syntax).
  • Search language hardening. $eq/$in/$ne are now exact and case-sensitive, with a new case-insensitive $eqic counterpart; a ? single-character wildcard joins the existing *; a quoted token bypasses wildcard interpretation entirely; $$ is the literal-dollar escape; operator names are case-insensitive; $regex gains an optional flags=i|m|s argument; SearchOperator is now immutable (create(...).build(), with copy() for a pre-filled builder) with a typed extension(Class<X>) hook replacing the untyped sql(Object) hook; parse failures throw BeanQuerySyntaxException with a specific Code; a shared JSON parity corpus keeps the server (Java) and client (juneau-search.js) engines byte-for-byte identical; and SearchType.bareHelp() adds per-type search help text, including a UTC-midnight clarification for bare TIMESTAMP values. See the Porting searches from another $-operator syntax note on the topic page below for migrating a case-insensitive $eq(...) search.
  • Postgres dialect and typed binds. PostgresDialect lives in its own module and package (juneau-beanquery-postgres, org.apache.juneau.beanquery.postgres). Search literals are parsed once per query by SearchType.parse(String) (NUMERIC to BigDecimal, BOOLEAN to Boolean, TIMESTAMP to OffsetDateTime/LocalDateTime/LocalDate) and exposed as SearchExpression.typedValue()/typedArgs(). A value that does not parse for its column type is BeanQuerySyntaxException.Code.BAD_VALUE (HTTP 400) in both the in-memory and SQL engines. SearchSqlRenderer and SqlDialect take typed Object values, and a custom operator opts in with SearchOperator.Builder.typedArgs(true). Relative-duration literals [+-]<n>(ms|s|m|h|d) work for NUMERIC and TIMESTAMP columns and resolve against a single per-query request time.
  • ISO-8601 durations in BeanQuery. Wherever a NUMERIC or TIMESTAMP column accepts a relative literal such as -24h, it now also accepts a signed ISO-8601 duration (PT24H, -PT24H, +PT30M, P1D) with identical semantics, in the in-memory and SQL engines and in juneau-search.js; invalid ISO text is BAD_VALUE. Existing literals and bare epoch milliseconds are unchanged.
  • Built-in SQL row mappers. SqlRowMapper.map() and SqlRowMapper.bean(Class) (records or setter beans), chosen automatically by SqlBeanQueryContext.Builder.build() when no rowMapper(...) is set.
  • In-memory and SQL parity. A SQL dialect that does not support an operator (such as $regex), or that does not declare supportsVersionOrdering() for the VERSION range operators, rejects that query with BAD_VALUE instead of silently returning different rows. PostgresDialect compares ENUM columns as text (wildcards included), compares VERSION columns as dotted-integer tuples, renders $regex with the POSIX ~/~* operators (mirroring flags=i|m|s; Postgres and Java regex syntax differ), and makes $not match NULL cells as the in-memory engine does.
  • BREAKING: PostgresDialect moved to org.apache.juneau.beanquery.postgres, and SearchSqlRenderer/SqlDialect.renderBare now receive typed Object values. See the Migration Guide.

See the new BeanQuery Package topic page.

juneau-microservice-jetty​

JettyMicroservice zero-config facade + bundled defaults​

juneau-microservice-jetty now ships a thin convenience facade, JettyMicroservice, that collapses the Microservice + JettyConfiguration bootstrap into a single static call, plus classpath defaults for jetty.xml and juneau.cfg. End result: stand up a Jetty-backed Juneau microservice with one Maven dependency and one @Bean Servlet.

public class App {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        JettyMicroservice.run(args, new RootResources()).join();
    }
}

Bundled classpath defaults (all overridable):

  • jetty.xml — single plain-HTTP ServerConnector on $S{availablePort,10000}. No resourceBase / WebAppContext / ResourceHandler filesystem mount is registered (no static-file serving by default). Servlets are auto-mounted by JettyServerComponent from @Bean Servlet contributions.
  • juneau.cfg — sections for [Jetty] (port, jetty.xml reference, var resolution), [REST] (default theme), [Console] (interactive console enabled with the standard exit / restart / help / config commands), [Logging] (logDir), and [SystemProperties] (Jetty SLF4J adapter wiring).

Override semantics are unchanged: a consumer-supplied jetty.xml or juneau.cfg on the working directory or earlier on the classpath wins, as does a @Bean JettyServerFactory / @Bean JettySettings in the consumer's @Configuration.

The JettyMicroservice.run(...) facade has three overloads:

  • run(String[] args, Servlet rootServlet) — interactive console enabled.
  • run(String[] args, Servlet rootServlet, boolean startConsole) — explicit console opt-in/out.
  • run(String[] args, WritableBeanStore beanStore, boolean startConsole, Class<?>... configurations) — power-user form for callers contributing multiple @Bean Servlets, custom MicroserviceListeners, or a parent bean store.

juneau-my-jetty-microservice retired (BREAKING)​

The legacy juneau-my-jetty-microservice template module has been removed from the reactor. Consumers should migrate to the new JettyMicroservice facade in juneau-microservice-jetty — it delivers the same zero-config developer experience without requiring the consumer to copy a template project.

ThemeMenuItem widget removed (BREAKING)​

org.apache.juneau.rest.server.widget.ThemeMenuItem and its $W{ThemeMenuItem} variable are gone, with no @Deprecated stage. Its links used a ?stylesheet= query parameter that nothing in the server ever read, so it never switched a page's theme. Remove it from @HtmlDocConfig(widgets, navlinks); to change the stylesheet, set @HtmlDocConfig(stylesheet) or the REST/theme config entry. See Stylesheets.

juneau-microservice-jetty / juneau-microservice-tomcat​

Graceful shutdown + readiness gating (zero-downtime k8s rollouts)​

Both embedded-server microservice flavors now perform a zero-downtime graceful shutdown suitable for rolling Kubernetes deployments, sharing one identical shutdown contract.

On shutdown, a shared ReadinessState flag is flipped before the listening connector stops, so GET /readyz immediately returns 503 (state=OUT_OF_SERVICE) while a load balancer / Kubernetes is still routing. GET /livez and GET /healthz stay healthy, so the orchestrator does not kill the pod mid-drain. The server then waits up to a bounded stopTimeout (default 30s) for in-flight requests to drain — Jetty via server.setStopTimeout(...), Tomcat by pausing the connector and waiting for the active request count to reach zero — with an optional shutdownSettleDelay between the readiness flip and the connector stop.

  • New shared org.apache.juneau.rest.server.health.ReadinessState flag, consulted by HealthAggregator to gate the READY probe (liveness and the aggregate health surface are unaffected).
  • New stopTimeout / shutdownSettleDelay knobs on both JettySettings and TomcatSettings, also configurable via juneau.cfg ([Jetty] / [Tomcat] sections, in milliseconds). Precedence: programmatic settings > config-file entry > (Jetty only: jetty.xml value) > 30s default.
  • Bundled juneau.cfg documents the knobs and the recommended Kubernetes preStop hook + terminationGracePeriodSeconds pairing.
  • MCP subscriptions/listen streams no longer hold the drain open. Those SSE streams never finish on their own, so a stop with any subscriber connected used to wait out the full stopTimeout (30s by default). ReadinessState gained onOutOfService(key, callback), servlets can opt in via the new ReadinessStateAware interface, and AbstractMcpRestServlet uses it to close its subscriptions (new McpSubscriptionBroker.closeAll(), a no-op by default) as soon as shutdown begins, so each stream sends its terminal frame and completes.
@Bean
JettySettings jettySettings() {
    return JettySettings.create()
        .stopTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(45))
        .shutdownSettleDelay(Duration.ofSeconds(2))
        .build();
}

See the new Graceful Shutdown & Readiness Gating topic page for details, including the Jetty/Tomcat parity table and Kubernetes deployment guidance.

Servlet filter registration for microservice apps​

A new ServletFilterRegistration bean mounts a jakarta.servlet.Filter on JettyServerComponent or TomcatServerComponent before the server starts, with URL patterns, explicit dispatcher types (REQUEST, FORWARD, ASYNC, ERROR) and a defined order relative to the auto-mounted AuthFilterChain. Previously only the REQUEST dispatch was reachable and only after start-up. The AuthFilterChain auto-mount now goes through the same ordered path. The petstore Jetty runner uses it for its console boundary and no longer wraps the root servlet.

On Tomcat, servlets mounted through TomcatServerComponent.addServlet are now async-capable (request.isAsyncSupported() is true), matching Jetty, so async @RestOp return types use the real async path instead of falling back to synchronous handling.

juneau-microservice-test (new module)​

@MicroserviceTest — whole-microservice JUnit 5 integration tests​

A new juneau-microservice-test module adds @MicroserviceTest, a JUnit 5 extension that boots a whole Microservice (config + lifecycle + embedded Jetty on an ephemeral port) for a test class — the standalone-microservice analog of Spring's @SpringBootTest.

  • Explicit SUT. Declare the system under test via @MicroserviceTest(configurations={...}) and/or a static Microservice.Builder microserviceBuilder() supplier method (no classpath scanning). The extension adds an ephemeral-Jetty Server (port 0) + JettyConfiguration automatically; Jetty for v1 (Tomcat pluggability is a follow-on).
  • Composes the existing @TestBean substrate (no parallel injection annotation). Default Mode INJECT installs overrides via Microservice.Builder.overridingBeanStore(...) before boot, so the service reads them from startup; Mode OVERLAY pushes/pops against the booted instance.
  • Parameter resolution for RestClient (bound to the booted root URL — the primary convenience), Microservice, WritableBeanStore, and the bound port.
  • Fresh instance per class, stopped cleanly in teardown (restart is unsupported); stop() restores process globals so multiple @MicroserviceTest classes are isolated within a JVM. The bound port is always read from the live ServerConnector.
  • Distinct from MockRestClient: use @MicroserviceTest for a real server/lifecycle over HTTP, MockRestClient for in-JVM single-resource tests.
  • This also added a small public composition entry point — JuneauBeanStoreExtension.discoverOverrides(...) — so other JUnit 5 extensions can reuse the @TestBean discovery without driving that extension's own lifecycle.

See the new Whole-Microservice Integration Tests (@MicroserviceTest) topic page.

Build & packaging (BOM + curated bundles)​

Published BOM + curated dependency bundles​

Juneau now publishes a Bill of Materials and a small set of curated dependency bundles so consumers can depend on a coherent, version-aligned slice of the framework without hand-maintaining <version> tags — while keeping Juneau's explicit-over-magic configuration model (no Spring-style classpath auto-configuration).

  • org.apache.juneau:juneau-bom (packaging pom) — import it (scope=import, type=pom) and drop explicit versions from your Juneau dependencies. Enumerates the consumer-facing Juneau modules plus the small set of starter-relevant third-party versions the bundles need (micrometer-core, opentelemetry-api, jakarta.servlet-api, jakarta.validation-api). It is not a whole-world third-party BOM, so it won't collide with a third-party BOM you import yourself.
  • Three deployment-shape bundles (packaging pom) — depend on one and transitively pull a coherent module set plus juneau-rest-client:
    • juneau-microservice-jetty-bundle
    • juneau-microservice-tomcat-bundle
    • juneau-springboot-bundle
<dependencyManagement>
    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.apache.juneau</groupId>
            <artifactId>juneau-bom</artifactId>
            <version>10.0.0</version>
            <type>pom</type>
            <scope>import</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>
</dependencyManagement>

The bundles are dependency aggregators only — they register no configurations and perform no classpath auto-discovery. Configuration registration stays explicit via Microservice.Builder.configurations(Class<?>...). This is a deliberate design choice: per the maintainer, "I actually see auto-configuration as a weakness in Spring Boot that leads to applications with long startup times and impossible-to-understand architectures." These bundles are also distinct from the clone-and-go juneau-microservice-*-starter templates, which live as true-orphan branches of apache/juneau (microservice-jetty-starter, microservice-tomcat-starter, microservice-springboot-starter). Clone with git clone -b microservice-jetty-starter --single-branch https://github.com/apache/juneau.git my-app (replace the branch name for the other two). See Starter Projects.

A reactor-consistency guard (scripts/check-bom-completeness.py, wired into the push gate) fails the build if a published module is missing from the BOM, so the enumeration can't silently drift. The binary distribution now also bundles juneau-microservice-tomcat (previously omitted).

See the new Dependency Management (BOM & Bundles) topic page for usage and the full explicit-over-magic rationale.

GraalVM native-image feasibility verdict + Docker layering guidance​

A feasibility assessment of GraalVM native-image support for Juneau's reflection-heavy marshalling/bean core landed a CONDITIONAL GO verdict: all reflection is funnelled through one wrapper layer (org.apache.juneau.commons.reflect.*, single setAccessible() choke point) with no Unsafe/MethodHandle/bytecode generation, and the BeanContext/ClassMeta model already computes the exact member set reachability metadata needs — making a Juneau-authored metadata emitter realistic. The maintainer-approved follow-on (a BeanContext-driven reachability-metadata.json emitter targeting the juneau-marshall core first, REST server deferred) is tracked as a dedicated committed work item; native-image builds of Juneau are not yet supported. The new topic page also documents Docker image-layering guidance for Juneau apps. See GraalVM Native Image & Docker Layering.

juneau-petstore (new module family)​

Three new modules under a top-level juneau-petstore/ aggregator together form the canonical Juneau petstore showcase application. The legacy juneau-examples-rest{,-jetty,-springboot,-jetty-ftest} family of modules has been retired in this release in favor of the petstore family — see the Breaking Changes section below.

juneau-petstore-core​

Shared, deployment-agnostic surface consumed verbatim by both the Jetty and Spring Boot deployments. Owns:

  • Domain beans — Pet, Order, User (plus Species/PetStatus/OrderStatus/UserStatus enums) under org.apache.juneau.petstore.dto. Plain Juneau beans, no JPA/Hibernate/Derby.
  • In-memory PetStore service — ConcurrentHashMap-backed, lazy-loads classpath seed JSON at petstore/init/{Pets,Orders,Users}.json via Json5Parser. Auto-IDs via AtomicLong.
  • PetStoreResource — full CRUD @Rest servlet (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE over /pets, /orders, /users). Uses org.apache.juneau.http.response.NotFound (next-gen) and @org.apache.juneau.http.Path/@Content. Spring-agnostic — extends BasicRestServlet so both deployments mount it identically.
  • View-engine demos — the Mustache and Freemarker subtabs of the console's rendering-flavors page (/console/dev/flavors/mustache, /console/dev/flavors/freemarker) demonstrate the typed-View return path through the juneau-rest-server-view-{mustache,freemarker} bridges. Pure-classpath engines so both deployments inherit view rendering at parity. (They replace the retired PetMustacheViewResource / PetFreemarkerViewResource.)
  • No-build React SPA demo — PetstoreUiResource mounts StaticFilesMixin to serve htdocs/petstore-ui.html, a single-page React UI that calls /petstore/pets over fetch(). Demonstrates the headless-JSON + decoupled-SPA pattern alongside the server-rendered HTML-doc UI; no Node/npm in the build and no network access needed (React and ReactDOM 18.3.1 are vendored under htdocs/vendor/, MIT-licensed, acknowledged in the root LICENSE; the app uses plain React.createElement, so there is no in-browser JSX compiler).
  • Secure demo + StubBearerTokenValidator — the console's bearer-token demo page (/console/dev/secure, with SecureApiRest) replaces the retired PetSecureResource (/petstore-secure/*); the auth-gated CRUD subset is gated by a BearerTokenGuard (fail-closed, op-level) backed by the in-memory stub validator. Demonstrates the bearer-token + @Auth Principal pattern; resource-Javadoc cross-references AuthFilterChain for multi-mechanism deployments.

juneau-petstore-jetty​

Jetty/Microservice deployment glue:

  • App.main calls Microservice.create().configurations(JettyConfiguration.class, AppConfig.class)....
  • RootResources extends BasicRestServletGroup — mounts every core child resource plus the Jetty-only Microservice admin trio (ConfigResource/LogsResource/ShutdownResource), sourced from the new juneau-microservice-examples module (see Breaking Changes below).
  • Bundled jetty.xml and juneau-petstore-jetty.cfg.
  • Starter-zip assembly — sources + cfg + jetty.xml for IDE-import use.
  • In-module integration tests (@JettyMicroserviceTest, ephemeral port).
  • Default URL: http://localhost:10000.

Launcher: python3 scripts/start-petstore-jetty.py.

juneau-petstore-springboot​

Spring Boot deployment glue:

  • App is a @SpringBootApplication with @Bean RootResources + @Bean ServletRegistrationBean<Servlet> mounted at /*.
  • RootResources extends BasicSpringRestServletGroup so child resources resolve as Spring beans (required for HelloResource's @Autowired HelloMessageProvider injection demo).
  • Inherits ${spring.version} from the repo parent.
  • application.properties configures port 5000.
  • spring-boot-maven-plugin repackage produces a runnable fat jar.
  • @SpringBootTest(webEnvironment=RANDOM_PORT) integration tests.
  • Default URL: http://localhost:5000.

Launcher: python3 scripts/start-petstore-springboot.py.

Parity story​

The core-hosted surface (CRUD, console, view demos, React SPA demo, auth-gated subset) is identical across both deployments by construction — it's shared code, not parallel copies. The deployment-specific surface (Jetty's microservice console + admin resources vs Spring Boot's @Autowired injection demo) is intentionally non-parity and documented as such.

Petstore admin console (/console)​

The petstore now ships a complete admin console at /console, built on console-ui and offered as the worked example for the framework pages. See juneau-petstore.

  • Fourteen pages (P1-P14). Each page has an FTL template and a Java builder twin (?builder), so the same page is shown both ways.
  • Server-mode tables driven by BeanQuery: filter, sort and page the pets, orders and users on the server.
  • Staged pet edits with the pending-changes badge (the photo field is excluded from staging).
  • Restock async job with a job-log card that follows the job as it runs.
  • Audit trail of console writes.
  • Custom cards. Petstore: kpi and inventory-gauge custom cards on /console/dev/cards demonstrate adopter card types.
  • Four rendering flavors (Builder, Html, Mustache and Freemarker) of the same pet list under /console/dev/flavors.
  • Bearer-token demo at /console/dev/secure, next to a CSRF boundary on /console/* in both deployments.
  • Tests. A Playwright browser harness exercises the pages, and FailLoud negative fixtures pin the error messages for mis-built pages.
  • Retired legacy resources. PetInfoResource, PetHtmlResource, PetSecureResource, PetMustacheViewResource and PetFreemarkerViewResource (and their /petstore-info, /petstore-html, /petstore-secure and /pet-views URLs) are gone, replaced by console pages. This is a breaking change for users of the sample only; the petstore is a sample, so it is not listed under Breaking Changes below.

Petstore legacy-surface completion​

The retired juneau-examples-rest family (see Breaking Changes below) carried six REST-servlet demonstrations that hadn't yet been ported into petstore or consciously dropped. That gap is now closed — three demos got petstore-flavored equivalents, and three were consciously dropped:

Ported to juneau-petstore-core, wired into both the Jetty and Spring Boot deployments:

  • AboutRest (/console/about, replacing the retired PetInfoResource at /petstore-info) — utility-beans demo: BeanDescription/Hyperlink/SeeOtherRoot rendered against the petstore's own Pet domain bean.
  • HtmlFlavorRest (/console/dev/flavors/html, replacing the retired PetHtmlResource at /petstore-html) — HTML5 bean-builder demo: a hand-built HTML5 Table fragment of all pets rendered from live petstore data.
  • GET/PUT /petstore/pets/{id}/photo (added to PetStoreResource) — image upload/serve demo, backed by new petstore-local PetPhotoSerializer/PetPhotoParser classes (org.apache.juneau.petstore.marshall) and wired to the previously-unused Pet.photo field.

Consciously dropped (not ported):

  • ATOM-feed DTO serialization demo — generic marshalling showcase with no petstore-domain tie-in; Atom (de)serialization itself remains exhaustively covered by juneau-bean-atom's own test suite and docs.
  • JSON-Schema DTO serialization demo — same shape as the Atom case; JSON-Schema generation is already exhaustively covered by juneau-bean-jsonschema's test suite and docs.
  • Server-Sent-Events demo — SSE transport mechanics are already integration-tested independent of any demo resource; a petstore-flavored SSE feature (e.g. live status updates) would be net-new feature work, out of scope for a port-or-drop cleanup.

The plan's remaining stretch scope — a @Remote typed-client demo and a Config API + SVL var-resolver showcase — was split out to a separate follow-on work item rather than folded in here.

juneau-rest-common / juneau-rest-server​

BeanQueryRequest request bean​

org.apache.juneau.http.BeanQueryRequest is a stock @Request class (a concrete BeanQuery subclass) that binds the usual list-fetch query parameters as a single method argument and feeds a BeanQuery session directly:

private static final InMemoryBeanQueryContext<Row> ROWS = InMemoryBeanQueryContext.create(Row.class).build();

@RestGet
public List<Row> getList(BeanQueryRequest q) {
    try (var s = ROWS.getSession(rows)) {
        return s.find(q).rows();
    }
}

Each getter binds one single-valued @Query whose wire name equals the property name: search, view (a column projection), sort, position, limit and opts (renamed from opt). The $-language and the key=value opts bag live inside those single strings and are decoded by the session, not on the wire. Each getter carries a @Schema description, so an operation taking a BeanQueryRequest documents all six parameters in Swagger automatically (position also declares minimum: 0).

A malformed query is reported as HTTP 400 with an X-BeanQuery-Error header and, with problem details on, a "code" member in the body; see Queryable rebuilt on the BeanQuery engine below. The @Request bean's constructor and setters are now verified when the operation table is built (see the Breaking Changes entry on request beans).

Apps add extras by subclassing BeanQueryRequest and redeclaring a getter with its own @Query name (e.g. @Query("v") getView()). Saved-view CRUD endpoints must not take BeanQueryRequest (view there is a saved-view id, not a column projection).

See the BeanQuery Package topic page.

@Request getters now honor collectionFormat=multi (getAll, not last-wins) and @Query(def=) / equivalent def= on the other part annotations, including Optional<T> returns.

Content Security Policy (CSP) support​

Juneau can now emit Content-Security-Policy response headers for the HTML it serves, including dynamic per-request nonce support. New in this release:

  • A first-class immutable ContentSecurityPolicy HTTP header bean + fluent builder in juneau-rest-common (org.apache.juneau.http.header), with typed directive setters (defaultSrc, scriptSrc, styleSrc, imgSrc, connectSrc, fontSrc, objectSrc, baseUri, frameAncestors, reportUri/reportTo), a generic directive(name, sources...) escape hatch, source-expression helpers, report-only mode, and a ready-made nonce-based "strict starter" preset.
  • Per-response SecureRandom nonce generation: the same nonce is injected into the emitted Content-Security-Policy header and stamped onto every inline <script>/<style> Juneau emits — the HtmlDoc template, the Swagger UI, the OpenAPI UI, and menu-item widgets.
  • Opt-in by design: turning CSP on is a deliberate, one-line choice; existing apps are unaffected by default.

See the new Content Security Policy topic page for details.

This feature was inspired by an earlier proposal from Gary Gregory (@garydgregory, PR #57); the implementation shipped here is a fresh one built against the current 10.0 APIs.

CSRF protection for apps that are not on loopback (CsrfBoundary)​

LoopbackBoundary protects an app only when every request arrives under one pinned Host over plain HTTP. A new CsrfBoundary in org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter covers everything else: an app reached under a real host name, over HTTPS, behind a proxy, or under more than one name.

  • Same-origin check with nothing pinned. On an unsafe request, Origin (with Sec-Fetch-Site as a fallback) must match the request's own scheme, host and port. A literal null origin is refused. Default ports are equated, and IPv6 literals are compared in bracketed form exactly as sent.
  • Header token. A browser request must also carry a per-session synchronizer token in a request header (X-Csrf-Token by default). HTML form posts cannot send a header, so they are unsupported by design.
  • Non-browser clients. A request with neither Origin nor Sec-Fetch-Site is admitted without a token only when a browser could not have sent it cross-site without a preflight (for client authors: send JSON, or send Origin plus the token). NonBrowser.REJECT and NonBrowser.REQUIRE_TOKEN tighten that.
  • Proxies. OriginSource.HOST_HEADER (the default) never reads X-Forwarded-*; OriginSource.CONTAINER takes the origin from the container's own forwarded-header support (Jetty ForwardedRequestCustomizer, Tomcat RemoteIpValve, Spring Boot forward-headers-strategy).
  • DNS rebinding. allowedHosts(...) refuses any request, safe ones included, whose host is not listed.
  • Applied by RequestBoundaryFilter, which works with either boundary. Register it at /* for REQUEST dispatches.
  • The microservice admin samples. AdminBoundary in juneau-microservice-examples registers a CsrfBoundary over ConfigResource, LogsResource and ShutdownResource, answering loopback host names only unless others are given, and the Jetty petstore installs it. See the microservice examples entry below.
  • Bus WebSocket handshakes. BusPolicy.boundary(...) now accepts a CsrfBoundary. A missing, null or malformed Origin is refused with HTTP 403 before the upgrade; a well-formed cross-site or mismatched Origin is refused after the upgrade with close code 4403, before any frame is sent or any bus session is touched. The handshake has no server name, so it judges the raw Host header (over HTTP/2, the request URI's authority) plus the request URI scheme, whatever OriginSource is set. Behind a proxy that rewrites Host with no container-side host rewriting, same-origin upgrades are refused; preserve Host at the proxy. BusWebSockets.register refuses any boundary type other than LoopbackBoundary and CsrfBoundary. Verified on Jetty and Tomcat; on Tomcat, RemoteIpValve forwards the scheme to the handshake but not the Host header, so a forwarded host is refused even with the valve's hostHeader set.
  • Opt-in trusted forwarded origin. CsrfBoundary.Builder.trustedForwarding(X_FORWARDED | FORWARDED) and trustedHops(n) let a boundary judge HTTP writes and bus WebSocket handshakes against the host and protocol a proxy you operate forwards, for deployments whose container does no forwarded-host handling. Off by default with no behavior change. Host and protocol are both required, the nth entry from the right is used, the forwarded origin replaces the container's rather than adding to it, and anything missing, malformed or in disagreement with the container is refused (seven new BoundaryReason values, HTTP 403; handshakes close with 4403). X-Forwarded-Port is never read.
  • Proxy allow-list for the forwarded origin. CsrfBoundary.Builder.trustedProxies(cidrs...) believes the forwarded header only from listed peer addresses (IPv4 and IPv6 ranges, validated at build; host bits are masked). Others carrying it are refused (FORWARDED_PEER_NOT_TRUSTED); others without it are judged as if forwarding were off. Off by default. HTTP where the container reports the TCP peer; WebSocket handshakes on Jetty; on Tomcat a forwarded handshake is refused while the list is set.

Behavior changes in the same work:

  • HTTP/2 requests with no Host header are judged on the container's :authority view. CsrfBoundary no longer refuses them with HOST_MISSING, and LoopbackBoundary no longer refuses them with HOST_MISMATCH. Bus WebSocket handshakes over HTTP/2 (RFC 8441 extended CONNECT, which Jetty enables by default with HTTP/2) are judged on their :authority instead of closing with 4403. Under HOST_HEADER, HTTP/2 requests are judged on the container's server name, which container forwarding support may rewrite. HTTP/1.x requests without Host are unchanged.
  • LoopbackBoundary judges the effective method. A GET carrying ?method=DELETE or an X-HTTP-Method-Override header now takes the write checks, even when the resource it reaches would not honor the override (it now does honor it where allowedMethodHeaders is set; see the next bullet).
  • Method overrides: all four headers honored, conflicts refused. X-HTTP-Method-Override, X-HTTP-Method and X-Method-Override are now honored under @Rest(allowedMethodHeaders) (and the global J_ALLOWED_METHOD_HEADERS), exactly as X-Method is; the setting is still empty by default, so applications that have not set it see no change. A request whose enabled override channels disagree (two different methods across ?method= and the headers, or repeated different values on one of them) is answered 400; identical repeats are fine. The method query parameter is now matched case-insensitively (?METHOD=PUT works) and read from the query string only, so a form-body method= field is no longer honored. The MCP bearer gate treats a POST claim on any of these channels as a POST.
  • BREAKING: method overrides on safe requests are restricted. A GET, HEAD, OPTIONS or TRACE request may now be overridden (through ?method= or any of the four override headers) only to a safe method (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE) or to a custom method whose operation is declared @RestOp(read=true). An override to any other method, for example GET ?method=DELETE, GET ?method=POST on an RRPC operation, or GET ?method=FOO reaching a method="*" operation, is refused with 405 Method Not Allowed and an Allow header, instead of being dispatched. Overrides on POST (for example POST ?method=PATCH for clients without PATCH) are unchanged. Defaults are unaffected: allowedMethodParams still defaults to HEAD,OPTIONS. Migration: mark read-only custom verbs @RestOp(read=true); change links that used ?method= to trigger a write into a POST (a form or a script), or call the method directly (curl -X DELETE); prefer path-based read links (/view/{file}) over ?method=VIEW, because a CSRF boundary still treats any custom-verb claim as a write. read=true on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/CONNECT, *, RRPC, or together with @Mutating fails at startup. An MCP server mounted as a mixin now answers an unauthenticated GET ?method=POST with 405 rather than 401. Every framework 405 now carries an Allow header, including the existing one for a path that matches under another method.
  • Rejections and token-bearing pages are no-store. A rejected request is answered with Cache-Control: no-store. Code that stamps a token into a response (ViewTable.CSRF_ATTR, RegionTable.of(region, csrfToken), PageSpec.csrf(...)) must call RequestBoundaryFilter.markTokenBearing(response), which sets Cache-Control: private, no-store.
  • No token in a committed response. A token is never embedded into a response that is already committed, including csrf attributes an author put on the page's body element. The page's writes then fail visibly.
  • Breaking (unreleased API): the nested LoopbackBoundary.Reason and LoopbackBoundary.Result types are now the top-level BoundaryReason and BoundaryResult, with no aliases. Code built against a 10.0.0 snapshot needs the new names.
  • Breaking (unreleased API): the rejection header is now X-Request-Boundary (it was X-Loopback-Boundary).

See REST Security and the Views Security Model.

Actuator-style management surface​

Juneau 10.0 adds a coherent, discoverable Actuator-style management surface while keeping Juneau's a-la-carte composability. Every endpoint ships in two independently-mountable flavors — a composable *Mixin and a routed *Resource sharing one worker — and a convenience BasicActuatorGroup assembles them under one configurable path prefix (default /actuator, overridable via the juneau.actuator.path system property).

New endpoints:

  • /info (juneau-microservice, org.apache.juneau.microservice.management) — renders the running application's ManifestFile main attributes (build/version/git metadata). Degrades to {} when no manifest is registered. Build-time git/version stamping goes in the consumer's application-jar build (a git-commit-id + maven-jar-plugin recipe is in the topic page).
  • /loggers (juneau-rest-server, org.apache.juneau.rest.server.management) — read all logger levels and (deny-by-default) set a level at runtime. Drives java.util.logging by default; Logback / Log4j2 backends are an explicit opt-in (see the dedicated entry below).
  • /metrics (juneau-rest-server-metrics-micrometer) — renders a Prometheus scrape from a consumer-provided Micrometer MeterRegistry resolved from the bean store; degrades to 501 when no scrapeable registry is present. Never auto-registers a default registry.
  • /threaddump + /heapdump (juneau-rest-server) — server-agnostic ThreadMXBean thread dump and HotSpot .hprof heap dump, both deny-by-default on security grounds (opt in via DumpsSettings).

Exposure is on-by-default-with-gating: non-sensitive reads are exposed; mutating/sensitive operations (/loggers set-level, the dumps) are deny-by-default behind explicit opt-in settings beans (LoggersSettings, DumpsSettings). No auth provider is auto-wired — the consumer supplies their own guard.

BasicActuatorGroup mounts only /healthz//readyz//livez and the dumps by default; /info and /loggers are off. The convenience group composes HealthMixin + DumpsMixin only — InfoMixin and LoggersMixin are deliberately left out, since an unauthenticated manifest dump (/info) and logger-topology disclosure (/loggers read) are both meaningful information leaks with no guard auto-wired. Re-enable either (or both) with an a-la-carte subclass adding @Rest(mixins={InfoMixin.class, LoggersMixin.class}) (additive to the inherited mixins). Applications that mount InfoMixin/LoggersMixin directly (not through BasicActuatorGroup) are unaffected.

See the new Management Surface topic page for the endpoint catalog, the BasicActuatorGroup one-liner, the exposure policy, and the manifest-stamping recipe.

/loggers non-JUL backends (Logback, Log4j2)​

The /loggers endpoint (above) now drives a pluggable LogBackend instead of being hardwired to java.util.logging. juneau-rest-server still ships only the JUL backend (JulLogBackend, the default) so the core stays dependency-free, and a new opt-in juneau-rest-server-management-logging module adds LogbackLogBackend + Log4j2LogBackend (the backends declared provided, so they never leak transitively).

  • Explicit selection (no classpath auto-detection, per the explicit-over-magic principle): declare the backend on the existing settings bean — LoggersSettings.create().backend(new LogbackLogBackend()).build().
  • Identical response shape across backends: read reports the configured level (empty string = inherited from an ancestor; ROOT key for the root logger); set is process-lifetime-only (no config-file rewrite). Level names are backend-native; an invalid name fails 400.
  • Drives the concrete backend, not the SLF4J facade: LogbackLogBackend for SLF4J→Logback, Log4j2LogBackend for Log4j2; an slf4j-jdk14 binding is JUL, so the default backend already covers it. Custom backends implement LogBackend directly.

This closes the 174b JUL-only /loggers limitation. See the extended Management Surface topic page.

Host-side mixin overrides — @Rest(mixinDefs=@Mixin(...))​

@Rest(mixins=...) lets a mixin class declare its own @Rest settings that apply only to its endpoints — but the composition decision often belongs to the host. New in 10.0.0, the @Rest(mixinDefs=@Mixin(...)) attribute lets a host declare a mixin and override selected @Rest-level settings for that mixin's endpoints, in one place, without editing or subclassing the mixin:

@Rest(mixinDefs=@Mixin(type=AdminResource.class, guards=AdminGuard.class))
public class ApiResource extends BasicRestServlet { ... }
  • Additive / non-breaking. mixinDefs coexists with the existing mixins=Class<?>[]; a @Mixin(type=X.class) with no overrides is exactly equivalent to a bare mixins=X.class entry, and existing usages are untouched.
  • Override slots mirror the composition-shaped @Rest attributes: guards, roleGuard/rolesDeclared, converters, encoders, serializers/parsers, responseProcessors, restOpArgs, partSerializer/partParser, messages, the default request/response headers + attributes, produces/consumes/defaultAccept/defaultContentType/defaultCharset, and maxInput.
  • Precedence: the host override layers on top of the inherited host chain (list-shaped props append, replace-shaped props win) and wins over the mixin class's own declaration. @Mixin carries its own noInherit (unioned with the mixin class's @Rest(noInherit=...)) so the host override is authoritative but overridable by noInherit.
  • Host-chosen re-mount: @Mixin(path=...)/paths={...} re-mount the mixin's endpoints under host-chosen prefix(es), reusing the existing pathToken normalization.
  • Transitive mixins are overridden only when separately named.

Internally this also normalized mixin discovery (one ResolvedMixin carrier for both bare and rich forms) and replaced the RestContext.Args boolean mixinContext flag with a typed ContextKind discriminator (Root/Child/Mixin). See Host-side overrides with @Mixin.

Mixin-declared response-processor fold — @Rest(mergeResponseProcessorsIntoHost=true)​

By default a mixin's responseProcessors apply only to the mixin's own endpoints — a host's own @RestOp methods see only the host's chain. The host-side @Mixin(mergeIntoHost=true) directive can fold all of a mixin's list-shaped attributes into the host, but it must be spelled out at every use-site. New in 10.0.0, a mixin class can declare @Rest(mergeResponseProcessorsIntoHost=true) on itself, so that a plain @Rest(mixins=ThatMixin.class) reference automatically folds only the mixin's responseProcessors into the host's own chain:

@Rest(responseProcessors=FreemarkerViewRenderer.class, mergeResponseProcessorsIntoHost=true)
public class FreemarkerMixin { ... }
  • Opt-in and non-silent. Defaults to false; only a mixin that declares it changes behavior. Mixins that don't keep today's isolated scoping exactly — no change to the default for arbitrary existing mixins.
  • Response-processor-scoped. Folds only responseProcessors — never guards, serializers, or any other list-shaped attribute (the narrower, mixin-declared counterpart to the host-side, fold-everything @Mixin(mergeIntoHost=true)). Same-class de-duplication applies.
  • View mixins opt in. All four view-renderer mixins — FreemarkerMixin, JspMixin, MustacheMixin, ThymeleafMixin — now declare it, so a bare @Rest(mixins=FreemarkerMixin.class) (etc.) renders the host's own View returns through the engine with no mergeIntoHost or explicit responseProcessors= ceremony.

See REST Server — Mixin Sub-Contexts and FreeMarker View Support.

Host-side child seeding — @Rest(childrenDefs=@Child(...))​

Children are deliberately isolated from the host's resolution chain — a child's serializers, parsers, guards, part serializer, etc. resolve against its own RestContext only, never inherited from the parent. New in 10.0.0, the @Rest(childrenDefs=@Child(...)) attribute lets a host seed a curated set of settings onto a routed child's otherwise-isolated context, without editing the child class — the child-resource analog of the @Rest(mixinDefs=@Mixin(...)) attribute above:

@Rest(childrenDefs=@Child(type=AdminResource.class, partSerializer=AdminPartSerializer.class, guards=AdminBearerGuard.class))
public class ApiResource extends BasicRestServlet { ... }
  • Additive / non-breaking. childrenDefs coexists with the existing children=Class<?>[]; a @Child(type=X.class) with no seed members is exactly equivalent to a bare children=X.class entry, and if both name the same class the rich entry wins (the bare entry is upgraded in place).
  • Two seed-semantics buckets — since children are isolated by design, a seed can't "override" an inherited chain the way a @Mixin override does; it can only add to or fill gaps in the child's own config: additive-security (guards, converters, roleGuard, rolesDeclared) — the host's contribution is added alongside the child's own (list-shaped members prepend; the two role-based members AND-stack) and can never be removed or weakened by the child; child-wins scalars (partSerializer, partParser, defaultCharset, maxInput) — the seed is a fallback that applies only when the child leaves the property unset, and the child's own explicit @Rest declaration always wins.
  • noInherit cuts the seed too. A child's own @Rest(noInherit="<property>") suppresses the corresponding host-seeded value, for either bucket, so the child always stays in full control of its own configuration.
  • Survives lazy materialization — a seed applies to a @Rest(lazyChildren="true") child on first request exactly as it would to an eagerly-built one.
  • Not (yet) seedable: defaultAccept/defaultContentType were originally planned but dropped before shipping — they resolve through a shared first-wins mechanism that would make the seed win over the child's own value, the opposite of every other child-wins scalar's contract.

See Host-side seeding with @Child and REST Server — Children vs Mixins.

Child resources inherit their parent's @Bean group beans​

@Rest(children=...) child resources now see the @Bean methods and non-null @Bean fields declared on their parent (the "group"), instead of only the parent's bootstrap bean store. Each RestContext now has an inheritable bean store — its own @Bean results layered over its bootstrap store — and that store is used as the parent/bootstrap store of every child.

@Rest(children={PetResource.class, OrderResource.class})
public class RootResources extends BasicRestServletGroup {

   // One store shared by every child resource.
   @Bean
   public PetStore petStore() {
      return new PetStore();
   }
}
  • New API: RestContext.getInheritableBeanStore() returns the store a resource exposes to its children.
  • Transitive. Each child's inheritable store sits on top of its parent's, so a grandchild sees the beans of its parent, its grandparent, and so on up to the root (including any Spring context bridged in at the root).
  • Child wins. A child's own @Bean of the same type and name takes precedence over the inherited one.
  • Framework-managed beans stay per-context. Serializers, parsers, the call logger, RestChildren and similar are not exported; each child still builds its own from its own @Rest configuration.
  • Beans flow down only. A child's beans are never visible to its parent or siblings.

Custom observations + one-dependency OTLP export + log correlation​

Juneau 10.0 extends its request-boundary observability to cover custom (non-request) observations, ships a single OTLP export bundle, and adds OpenTelemetry trace-id log correlation — all keeping the explicit-over-magic, off-by-default contract (no classpath auto-configuration).

  • Custom-observation API (org.apache.juneau.rest.server.observation): a new explicit programmatic API — Observations.observe(name, tags) (try-with-resources Observation handle), an Observer that composes the existing SPIs, and non-request default methods on the two SPIs (MetricsRecorder.record(name, tags, elapsed, error) + TracerHook.startSpan(name)). Instruments an arbitrary block of work with a timer + span; reuses the exact request-path metricName/metricTags model. No @Observed annotation — Juneau has no AOP/method-interception substrate, so observation is an explicit block (consistent with the explicit-over-magic philosophy). No-backend path is zero-allocation. The Micrometer + OTel bridges override both default methods (OTel opens an INTERNAL-kind span, nested under any active request span).
  • juneau-observability-otlp-bundle: a curated dependency bundle (under juneau-bundles) that pulls both Juneau observability bridges plus a version-aligned OTLP exporter stack — opentelemetry-exporter-otlp (+ SDK + autoconfigure) for traces and micrometer-registry-otlp for metrics — in one dependency. Metrics + traces for v1 (OTLP logs export deferred). A dependency aggregator only; you still wire the @Bean MetricsRecorder/@Bean TracerHook explicitly.
  • Log correlation: the JUL LogEntryFormatter gains optional {traceId}/{spanId} placeholders, sourced reflectively from the active OTel Span.current() (no hard OTel dependency — they render empty when OTel is absent). MdcAsyncListener additionally folds the active trace/span id into the propagated SLF4J MDC snapshot (keys trace_id/span_id) so correlation survives the async-completion hop, gated by isMdcAsyncPropagation() and kept reflective. SLF4J→Logback/Log4j2 apps wire their own MDC pattern (JUL-only is a documented v1 limitation). This also fixed a latent multi-digit format-group bug in the LogEntryFormatter regex builder.

See the extended Observability — Micrometer + OpenTelemetry topic page.

Resource-level authentication — RestAuthenticator​

Juneau 10.0 adds a RestAuthenticator SPI (org.apache.juneau.rest.server.auth) — an ergonomic, in-resource way to resolve a request's Principal + roles so roleGuard, RoleBasedRestGuard, @Auth Principal, and req.isUserInRole(...) all work with no container-managed security and no servlet-layer filter. It complements the AuthN Filter Framework and reuses the same underlying auth implementations.

  • Shared Authenticator contract — a new Authenticator functional interface (Optional<AuthResult> authenticate(HttpServletRequest)) is now implemented by both AuthFilter and AuthFilterChain, so every existing filter (SAML / OAuth / JWT / API-key / bearer) is reusable verbatim at the resource layer. RestAuthenticator.of(Authenticator) adapts any of them.
  • AuthResult merge modes — AuthResult gains an immutable merge mode: of(...) = ADD (union roles, principal required — unchanged), ofRoles(...) = roles-only ADD (null principal — keeps the inherited identity), replacing(...) = REPLACE (swap identity outright). The existing of(...) factories and behavior are preserved (backward compatible).
  • Registration & DI — resolved per RestContext with precedence registered bean › @Bean method › @Rest(authenticator=...) › RestServlet.createAuthenticator(BeanStore). Both Authenticator-into-RestAuthenticator and RestAuthenticator-into-resource injection work through the bean store.
  • Inheritance & folding — unlike guards, authenticators inherit down the child-resource tree: a single root authenticator covers all descendants, which may augment (add roles), replace (swap identity), or opt out with @Rest(noInherit={"authenticator"}).
@Rest(children = { ChildResource.class })
public class RootResource extends BasicRestServlet {
    @Bean
    public RestAuthenticator authenticator(AuthFilterChain chain) {
        return RestAuthenticator.of(chain);  // covers root + all descendants
    }
}

See the new REST Authenticator — Resource-Level Authentication topic page.

Queryable rebuilt on the BeanQuery engine + juneau-rest-server-datatables (new module)​

Juneau 10.0 replaces Queryable's hand-rolled search/view/sort/paging code (ObjectSearcher/ObjectSorter/ObjectViewer/ObjectPaginator) with the shared BeanQuery engine, so one search language, one set of limits and one error model cover REST responses, DataTables server-side processing and SQL-backed queries. A new opt-in module also ships a DataTables server-side processing adapter plus browser-side helpers.

  • Queryable on BeanQuery — the search / view / sort / position / limit / opts request parameters (bound by BeanQueryRequest) run against an InMemoryBeanQueryContext built from the response's row type (one context per element class, cached for the life of the converter; Map rows get a per-request context). Example: GET /people?search=age=$gte(18)&sort=name,age:desc&view=name,age&position=20&limit=10. Non-tabular results are returned unchanged.
  • QueryableSettings — a bean-store-resolved per-resource bean (mirroring IntrospectableSettings) that tunes the context: defaultLimit (100), maxLimit (1000), allowRegex (on by default, allowRegex(false) opts out), regexTimeout, countPolicy, and the search-clause / sort-key / search-length / expression-depth caps. Unset settings keep the BeanQuery builder defaults.
  • Counts — ?opts=counts=true adds X-BeanQuery-Total and X-BeanQuery-Matched response headers (each only when that count was computed). The body stays a bare list.
  • Central error mapping — RestContext.convertThrowable maps BeanQuerySyntaxException to HTTP 400 with an X-BeanQuery-Error: <CODE> header (BeanQueryRequest.ERROR_HEADER) and, with problem details on, a "code" member in the body; BeanQueryExecutionException maps to HTTP 500 with the fixed body Query execution failed. (the cause is logged, never sent to the client). The DataTables adapter uses the same contract (next bullet).
  • juneau-rest-server-datatables module (org.apache.juneau:juneau-rest-server-datatables) — a new opt-in add-on (not bundled in juneau-distrib, mirroring the juneau-rest-server-management-logging precedent) with:
    • DataTablesQuery (org.apache.juneau.rest.server.datatables.adapter) — maps the DataTables server-side contract onto BeanQuery: DataTablesQuery.toBeanQuery(req, ctx) builds a BeanQuery from a DataTablesRequest (per-column search, order, paging, and a global search that expands to an $or of a per-SearchType leaf — $contains/$prefix/$eqic/$eq — over every searchable, resolvable column, not just text), and DataTablesQuery.run/runArrays execute it and map the result onto the DataTables envelope. The browser posts the draw state as JSON (not DataTables' default form-encoded request) through a new JuneauDataTables.ajax(url, extra?) helper in juneau-datatables.js, or the data-juneau-datatable-ajax auto-init attribute. A malformed request (unknown column, a maxSearchClauses/maxSortKeys cap exceeded, a bad search expression) raises BeanQuerySyntaxException, which the adapter does not catch: the central mapping answers HTTP 400 with an X-BeanQuery-Error: <CODE> header and the message in the body, exactly like any other Queryable endpoint. JuneauDataTables.ajax installs an xhr.dt listener that shows that server message through DataTables' normal error path (the error.dt event, then DataTable.ext.errMode) instead of a generic "Ajax error"; other failed requests keep the DataTables default. An execution failure is HTTP 500 via the central BeanQueryExecutionException mapping. See DataTables.
    • Views runtime server-mode tables now ride the same wire format. A juneau-rest-server-views table with dataMode: "server" now gets serverSide: true and ajax: JuneauDataTables.ajax(url, {...}) (in juneau-views.js: buildOptions → buildServerAjax) instead of a hand-built GET config, so there is one wire format end to end. Breaking for existing server-mode endpoints: they must now be @RestPost methods taking @Content DataTablesRequest, not GET handlers reading query-string parameters. Column-scoped ribbon options now ride the JSON body as that column's search.value (ribbonColumnSearches), $and-merged with the user's own search on the same column (mergeColumnSearches) — fixing a bug where such filters were silently dropped. param:-scoped ribbon options (ribbonQueryParams) and the nested-table parent-scope param (applyNestedScope) stay URL query parameters, re-derived on every request through beforeSend. Client-mode tables are unchanged. A page must load juneau-datatables.js before juneau-views.js; otherwise server mode fails loudly (a warning) instead of silently falling back to GET. See DataTables.
    • DataTablesResults<T> — the {draw,recordsTotal,recordsFiltered,data} (+ optional error) envelope bean, rendered by the negotiated serializer (no hardcoded JSON).
    • Browser-side helpers — DataTablesColumns (generate columns:[…] from bean-property order + @Schema titles), DataTablesTable (build a DataTables-ready HTML5 Table DOM bean, with MarshallingContext overloads), and DataTablesMixin (serves a first-party juneau-datatables.js auto-init glue script). DataTables' own JS/CSS and jQuery remain caller-provided (not vendored — their license is not ASF category-A).

Themeable admin-console chrome + FreeMarker macro composition (new modules: juneau-rest-server-console-ui, -console-ui-freemarker)​

Juneau 10.0 adds two opt-in modules that give an admin-console-style resource a themeable CSS "chrome", an enum status/domain pill component, and (for FreeMarker consumers) macro-based composition — without pulling a template engine or the DataTables add-on into juneau-rest-server core. The two modules form an acyclic dependency chain (console-ui → console-ui-freemarker); a chrome-only consumer never drags in FreeMarker or DataTables transitively.

  • juneau-rest-server-console-ui — ConsoleChromeMixin serves a dynamically themed chrome.css (the module's shipped structural stylesheet plus a :root block built from validated --jc-* theme tokens); Theme validates every token value through a normalize-then-accept-known-safe pipeline (reject C0/C1/DEL control chars → strip CSS comments → case-insensitively reject any url( production → match an allowlist grammar for colors/fonts/lengths/gradients) rather than a denylist, so a token value can never smuggle a url()-based injection. Color/font/length tokens sink only into non-URL-capable CSS properties; the sole URL-capable sink (background-image, for --jc-page-bg/--jc-avatar-bg) is unreachable via url() anyway since the grammar structurally excludes that production. The console logo is a static chrome.css constant, not a configurable token. The reusable enum pill/badge component (<span class="tag <domain> <value>">) is rendered by the <@tag domain=... value=.../> FreeMarker macro in the console base.ftlh (see Admin Console Chrome).
  • Console theming is FTL-only: custom palettes are authored with <@theme>/<@token> (value= for leaves, alias= for live var() references). ThemePack, ThemeSettings, ThemePackSettings, ConsoleChromeMixin.Builder.pack(...)/pageBackgroundImage(...) and the /juneau-console/assets/logo/page-bg endpoints were removed; ConsoleChromeMixin.create().theme("<stock-name>") selects a stock palette for the served chrome.css.
  • Page Tabs and Page Subtabs — a Page Tab is 38.5px tall: a 3px accent border, 8px/10px padding, and 13px text at line-height 1.5. A Page Subtab is 30px tall. The selected Page Tab and the selected Page Subtab are bold. The box is themeable through --jc-nav-tab-padding-block, --jc-nav-tab-padding-inline, --jc-nav-tab-line-height, --jc-page-nav-child-padding-block and --jc-page-nav-child-padding-inline.
  • <@console theme="<stock-name>"> still selects a built-in stock theme (an unknown name is rejected fail-closed); a nested <@theme name=> inside the directive overrides it.
  • The juneau-rest-server-theme-packs module was removed.
  • juneau-rest-server-console-ui-freemarker — ConsoleFreemarkerMixin extends FreemarkerMixin (register it typed as FreemarkerMixin, mirroring the load-bearing-return-type rule FreemarkerMixin beans already follow) augments the resolved Configuration's TemplateLoader with a second, classpath-root-rooted ClassTemplateLoader, without shadowing the consumer's own basePath-relative templates. This resolves the reserved org/apache/juneau/console/base.ftlh template (pulled in via a loader-root-absolute <#include "/org/apache/juneau/console/base.ftlh">) and its <@tag domain=... value=.../> macro — the trusted-HTML adapter for the pill component above. A consumer-supplied Configuration bean (Spring Boot autoconfig, etc.) is honored untouched, not augmented.
  • DataTablesTable additive @Html(render=...) honoring (in the existing juneau-rest-server-datatables module) — DataTablesTable.of(MarshallingContext, String, Collection<?>, Class<?>) now resolves and applies each row property's @Html(render=...) the same way the ordinary HtmlSerializer/HtmlDocSerializer path already does, so a column whose bean property declares a custom @Html(render=...) (for example an enum rendered as a status pill) renders through it instead of as a raw enum name. This is not a purely-additive change: a bean already using @Html(render=...) for the existing serializer path now also renders through that same render when passed through this DataTablesTable overload, where it previously rendered the raw value. Map-based rows are unaffected (no BeanPropertyMeta to resolve a render from).
  • juneau-rest-server-console-ui-freemarker — shareable-URL state and more datatables catalog keys. The views toolkit pack now includes juneau-urlstate.js (after juneau-pagestate.js), so the View Settings Copy link button and shareable-URL state work on <@page toolkit="views"> pages without loading the script by hand. <@card type="datatables"> catalogs now pass copyLink, rowActions, rowClassRules and pausePollingWhileEditing through onto the view, and selection and bulk through onto the slot; previously these keys were silently dropped on FTL-built pages.
  • juneau-rest-server-views / TableSpec — urlState key and the day(YYYY-MM-DD) directive. A table view can now opt in to built-in shareable-URL directives with TableSpec.urlState(String...) (or urlState: {day: {}} in a catalog; the page schema validates it). day stores a calendar date in ?state= and passes it to the server as a day query parameter (rename it with TableSpec.urlStateDayParam(String param), emitted as urlState.day.param) so a resource can return that day's [start, end) window; malformed dates are ignored. Views without the key are unchanged.
  • juneau-rest-server-console-ui-freemarker — open card-type registry. Unknown well-formed card types now pass through the server, and the JS shell fails them with E-JS-4. <@card> gains a src= attribute. A bare-URL datatables body is removed (it is now E-25), and searchType validation moves to render time (E-32). The bulk wire contract is "2" (aggregate mode, BulkResult). <@card type="datatables"> is the one table surface.
  • QuickStat gains meter and segmented kinds. QuickStat.meter(id, label, value, max) paints a filled track with role="meter", and QuickStat.segmented(id, label).segment(...) paints a proportional bar with a text legend. Both require a non-blank label. The new statusTone(StatusTone) sets an item tone from the shared status palette; tone(QuickStat.Tone) is unchanged.
  • Inline datatables catalogs refuse a malformed quickStats strip (E-37). This includes an off-palette tone on any item, plain tiles included. Such tones used to be dropped silently by the client.

See the new Admin-Console Chrome topic page.

Console page contract and JS shell​

<@console> pages now carry a versioned JSON page contract (#juneau-page, schema juneau-page.schema.json) and load one shell script, /juneau-console/juneau-console.js, which draws the header, nav (any depth, aria-current from activeNav or a segment-aware URL fallback), cards and footer. The server keeps rendering <head>.

  • New: PageContractAssert (published test helper), ConsoleTemplateValidator (static template lint), ConsoleFreemarkerMixin.Builder.devMode(boolean) (schema validation at render time), jcHasToolkit(name), <@footer text="…"/>, and window.JuneauConsole (contract, card, registerCard, mount, chrome, and the juneau:console-mounted event).
  • Loud failures: template mistakes fail the render with E-1 to E-18; contract problems in the browser show a .jc-console-error banner (E-JS-1 to E-JS-12, then E-JS-14).
  • Fix: a @Bean returning ConsoleFreemarkerMixin (rather than FreemarkerMixin) is now found; previously it silently fell back to the default mixin without the console directives.
  • BREAKING (10.0 snapshots only): the page contract's top-level version key is renamed contractVersion, matching every other Juneau envelope contract (ModalDef, FormDef, BarSlot, ActionResult, RegionDef, the card/slot envelopes). The value is unchanged ("1"). There is no fallback: juneau-page.schema.json now requires contractVersion and forbids version, juneau-console.js reads only contractVersion (JuneauConsole.SUPPORTED_VERSIONS is now SUPPORTED_CONTRACT_VERSIONS), PageContractAssert.hasVersion(String) is renamed hasContractVersion(String), and assertPage(...) throws if a contract still carries version. Pages are generated by <@console>, so upgrading Juneau is the only step; code that hand-builds a page contract, or calls hasVersion, must be updated. Browsers that cached the previous juneau-console.js (served with a one-day max-age) show an E-JS-2 banner until the cache expires or the page is hard-reloaded.
  • BREAKING: the FTL globals pageBody, pageTab, pageInit, pageCss, pageToolkit, pageToolkitCss, pageToolkitJs and pageThemeCss are removed (use jcHasToolkit("views")). The legacy chrome templates that did not use <@console> are removed; a <@page> whose chrome renders no <@console> is an error. The <@card> types js, json and calendar are removed (use type="html" with a body or a registered card type), as are the data-juneau-card-sidecar scripts (no directive emits them any more; the orphaned juneau-page-cards.js asset is deleted). juneau-chrome.js is absorbed into juneau-console.js. Server HTML no longer contains nav, header, footer or card wrappers; tests that matched that HTML must move to PageContractAssert.

Card asset dependencies​

Console cards now declare the scripts and stylesheets they need, and <@page> loads each one once, in dependency order. See Card Asset Dependencies.

  • New: ToolkitPack (packs with dependsOn and a VENDOR / RUNTIME kind), the built-in packs jquery, datatables, datatables-glue and datatables-buttons, <@card requires=...>, and ConsoleFreemarkerMixin.Builder methods registerToolkitPack(ToolkitPack), cardRequires(type, packs...) and providedPacks(names...). build() fails on an unknown pack, a cycle, or a VENDOR pack depending on a RUNTIME pack.
  • New: <@card class="..."> adds one or more CSS classes to the card's wrapper element, so a page can keep its own scope class on the card. Each name must be a plain CSS class token or the render fails. See Admin Console Chrome.
  • New: WebJarsMixin and WebJarResolver in juneau-rest-server serve /webjars/* from the classpath. juneau-rest-server-datatables now depends on the jQuery and DataTables WebJars (DataTables 2.3.8, Buttons 3.2.6, jQuery 3.7.1).
  • Changed: every <@card type="datatables"> loads jQuery, DataTables and juneau-datatables.js, in client and server mode. Previously the glue loaded only for server-mode cards and the page had to load jQuery and DataTables itself. A host with datatables cards composes WebJarsMixin as well as DataTablesMixin.
  • BREAKING (10.0 snapshots only): juneau-datatables.js left the views pack. ToolkitPackRegistry.Resolved is split into vendorCss, vendorJs, runtimeCss and runtimeJs, and the resolve(names, req, boolean) overload is removed. A page that loads jQuery or DataTables through <@scripts phase="after-toolkit"> must drop those tags (they would load twice, after the glue). A copy loaded through init= or css= is skipped only when its file name matches the pack's; an app with its own copies should name the packs in providedPacks(...) or mount WebJarsMixin.
  • Removed (10.0 snapshots only): APIs left unused once every consumer moved to card-declared packs. DataTablesMixin.JQUERY_CDN_URL, DATATABLES_JS_CDN_URL and DATATABLES_CSS_CDN_URL are gone; jQuery and DataTables now come from the WebJars. PageCapture.hasServerModeTable() is gone, because every datatables card now requires the datatables-glue pack.
